title: Neurofeedback training with motor imagery in stroke patients at home and associated changes in functional connectivity
summary: After a stroke, many people struggle with performing movements as they did before. One promising rehabilitation method is motor imagery (MI) training, where individuals mentally imagine movements instead of physically performing them. This technique can be enhanced by neurofeedback (NF), which provides real-time feedback on brain activity. In this study, we investigate whether a four-week home-based MI-NF training program can help improve motor control of the arms and hands. Participants are grouped based on the location of their brain lesion and are closely monitored throughout the study. Before, during, and after the training, we measure various physical and neurological parameters, including muscle strength, brain activity, and movement execution. Our goal is to determine whether and how MI-NF training can enhance brain plasticity and support motor recovery after stroke. The findings from this study could help develop new therapeutic approaches in neurorehabilitation.
conditions: Motor impairment of one side of the body after stroke

interventions.name: Neurofeedback-training based on motor imagery (14 sessions over four weeks of 45 min. training) as a multiple baseline design.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
First-time stroke, chronic stage (at least six months after the stroke), permanently reduced mobility of an upper limb, physical and mental suitability
Exclusion criteria:
Moderate to severe aphasia, apraxia, neglect, other serious physical or mental illness in addition to stroke, complete loss of mobility of an upper limb, unsuitability for MRI scans (metallic objects in the body, pregnancy, claustrophobia), sleep deprivation (< than four hours sleep), drug use, use of medication affecting the central nervous system, simultaneous participation in another study on stroke
